title: Shortcut Learning in Feature-Based Algorithm Selection
abstract: arXiv:2611.20440v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Landscape features give learning models information about the objective function for algorithm selection, algorithm configuration, and performance prediction. Should these features capture more information? Not always, because a model may rely on information that the algorithms ignore. This phenomenon is called shortcut learning, and in-distribution accuracy can hide it. We propose the Rubber Ruler Test. It transforms the objective values of test instances with random strictly increasing transformations, reruns the algorithms, and measures prediction performance. Comparison-based algorithms such as CMA-ES perform identically after the transformation, so for them any drop reveals shortcut learning. On 10-dimensional BBOB, a model for two comparison-based algorithms learned shortcuts even from normalized objective values. The R^2 of a model using all ELA features dropped from 0.85 to 0.23, below 0.45 with invariant features only. Rank-ba

translated_title: 基于特征的算法选择中的捷径学习
translated_abstract: 景观特征为学习模型提供关于目标函数的信息，可用于算法选择、算法配置和性能预测。这些特征是否应该捕获更多信息？答案并非总是肯定的，因为模型可能依赖于算法本身所忽略的信息。这种现象被称为捷径学习，而分布内准确率可能会掩盖这一问题。我们提出了橡皮尺测试：该方法通过随机严格单调递增变换来改变测试实例的目标值，重新运行算法，并测量预测性能的变化。对于CMA-ES等基于比较的算法，变换后其表现完全不变，因此对它们而言，任何预测性能的下降都揭示了捷径学习的存在。在10维BBOB基准测试中，针对两个基于比较算法的模型即使仅使用归一化目标值也会学到捷径。使用全部ELA特征的模型R²从0.85降至0.23，低于仅使用不变特征时的0.45。Rank-ba…（原文摘要被截断）
tldr: 提出橡皮尺测试，通过随机单调变换目标值来检测基于特征的算法选择模型中的捷径学习，发现模型即使使用归一化目标值也会学到算法忽略的信息，导致预测性能大幅下降。
en_tdlr: Proposes the Rubber Ruler Test to detect shortcut learning in feature-based algorithm selection by applying random monotonic transformations to objective values, revealing that models learn shortcuts even from normalized objective values, with R² dropping from 0.85 to 0.23.
